title: CAP Theorem
description: A three-replica seat-reservation service splits into a two-node majority and an isolated node. Selling a seat twice is unacceptable. Which statement describes a CP policy during this partition?

options.text: A system can guarantee all three: Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance
options.explanation: The CAP theorem proves that in the presence of a network partition, a distributed system must choose between consistency and availability — it cannot guarantee all three simultaneously.

options.text: During a network partition, a CP system sacrifices availability to maintain consistency
options.explanation: A quorum-based CP operation can continue on the majority side while rejecting or blocking on the isolated side. It sacrifices availability for requests that cannot reach the authority, not necessarily for every request. Database behavior depends on operation and configuration.

options.text: AP systems never return stale data
options.explanation: An AP operation can keep answering from reachable replicas during a partition, accepting stale reads or conflicting writes that need reconciliation. Do not infer this policy for every operation from a database brand name.

options.text: The CAP theorem only applies to SQL databases
options.explanation: CAP applies to ALL distributed data stores regardless of data model — SQL, NoSQL, key-value, document, etc.
